season.evidence: Stored Jun-Sep looks late. Logged routes 'White Salmon Glacier'/'WSG'/'White Salmon' show successful ascents in Mar (2), Apr (3), May (1), Jun (1), all but one on skis. Web search: ski-route trip listings from February and April, and a note that in summer the approach is a long brushy bushwhack. So the practical window is spring snow.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Positive identity (logged as this route, camp near the glacier toe, summit and ski descent) and in season (Mar 28, within a month of April). But the track starts at the ski-area day lodge, 724 m from our stored hairpin pin and is not a round trip by the 300 m rule. The day lodge is a real, separate winter start (mapped at 48.86196,-121.65385, Nominatim), not the 'old lodge site' our text names, so I am not moving the pin. Owner may accept it as a winter-start track.

facts.text: In early April a big avalanche debris field can choke the White Salmon creek drainage; budget about an hour to wind through it

In early April with a deep base the glaciers can be travelled unroped; crampons came out for the Upper Curtis Glacier and the upper part of Hell's Highway, and the snow in the summit gully was firm at midday.
In April the narrowest part of the final summit gully was easier on the climber's left than on the right.
two ice axes (April, firm snow on the summit gully)

season.evidence: Stored Jul-Sep kept. Logged 'SE Ridge'/'Fisher Chimneys, SE ridge' ascents fall in Jun (rare), Jul and Aug mostly, a few Sep. Web: park ranger conditions pages say the SE ridge is mostly snow-covered in mid-June and close to snow-free by late July; a guided late-August trip found good rock and snow cover to the base.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Logged 'Fisher Chimneys + SE Ridge (5.3)', Aug 10, summited, a full car-to-car round trip, and the report names the ridge, pitches and a 5.3 crux, so the identity of the finish is positive. Not assigned because (a) it starts at the Lake Ann trailhead (about 10.4 km from our Shannon Ridge pin) and (b) the same ascent also fits the stored Fisher Chimneys route, so it may be one line filed twice. facts.text: By mid-August one stretch of the forest road to the Shannon Ridge trailhead is washed out and high clearance helps; the trail up the ridge is cleared and easy to follow, and the glacier's lowest slope is hard ice at dawn after a cold night, with crevasses right away and no set bootpack.
In mid-June the snow is continuous from about 4,700 ft and the basin camp near 6,200 ft has running water and dry pads; slopes above camp can shed wet avalanches onto the trail on the way out.
Rope drag in the summit gully can knock loose plate-sized rocks onto the rappeller below in August
In early August a single rack of nuts, a few cams and slings was enough on the ridge; the first pitch can be simul-climbed and the rest belayed.
A pair of ropes rappelled double speeds the gully descent when other parties are queuing, and a lone single-rope rappel followed by two double-rope ones got a party down in August.

notes: Seven routes were in the packet; none gets a track. Fisher Chimneys and Sulphide Glacier already have tracks and are not in this list. The strongest unassigned candidate is 3305030 (Aug 10 2026, Fisher Chimneys + SE ridge 5.3, complete from Lake Ann): our SE-corner route's own overview says it is climbed after a Fisher or Sulphide approach, so this is arguably the route's full line, but it also fits the Fisher Chimneys route and starts away from the stored Shannon Ridge pin. Likewise 3150780 and 2803453 (March/April ski ascents) are positively the White Salmon Glacier but start at the ski-area day lodge (48.86196,-121.65385, confirmed by a Nominatim search for White Salmon Day Lodge) rather than our hairpin pin 724 m away; our WSG stored season Jun-Sep looks too late (logged ascents Mar-Jun, mostly skied). Hanging Glacier, North Face, NE Ridge, NW Arete and Price Glacier have no tracks on Peakbagger for these lines in the harvest.
